wines.name: Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blend: 82% Cabernet Sauvignon, 9% Petit Verdot, 7% Malbec, 2% Merlot
wines.about: Chappellet has farmed the steep, rocky slopes of Pritchard Hill since 1967, and its Signature Napa Valley Cabernet has been the family's flagship wine for more than three decades.

web.note: Dark and concentrated, with aromas of blackcurrant, dark cherry and plum layered with cedar, mountain sage, tobacco and toasted oak. The palate feels silky and seamless, with black cherry, chocolate and espresso flavors, while fresh herbs and baking spice keep it lively through a long, resonant finish.
web.sourceName: Chappellet 2022 Signature Cabernet Sauvignon winemaker notes

wines.name: Saint-Julien Grand Cru Classé
wines.flag: Cellaring for the long haul, still closed.
wines.blend: 72% Cabernet Sauvignon, 25% Merlot, 3% Cabernet Franc
wines.about: A Second Growth in the 1855 classification and one of the largest estates in St-Julien, Gruaud Larose still carries its old motto on the label: the wine of kings, the king of wines.

web.note: A polished, deep St-Julien that opens with wild berries, plum and cassis alongside licorice, dried flowers, cedar and a pencil-shaving edge. Medium to full-bodied and remarkably refined, it pairs real concentration with fine, powdery tannins and bright acidity, finishing long and savory. It will reward a few more years in the cellar.

wines.name: Pauillac Grand Cru Classé
wines.blend: 72% Cabernet Sauvignon, 20% Merlot, 6% Cabernet Franc, 2% Petit Verdot
wines.about: A Fifth Growth Pauillac next door to Mouton Rothschild and Pontet-Canet, Pedesclaux has been transformed since the Lorenzetti family bought it in 2009, with a striking glass-walled gravity-flow cellar and steadily rising quality.

web.note: Fragrant and inviting, with violets, warm cassis, ripe plum and licorice joined by hints of dark chocolate, cherry and cinnamon spice. Medium to full-bodied, it offers juicy black and red fruit supported by ripe, finely grained tannins and lively freshness, closing on a long, perfumed finish.
web.sourceName: Millesima (blend, critic scores and tasting notes)

wines.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.jakeNote: Reliable, if not thrilling. A dependable weeknight bottle.
wines.blend: 94% Cabernet Sauvignon, 6% Merlot
wines.about: Decoy is the approachable everyday label from the Duckhorn family of wines, first made by Dan and Margaret Duckhorn more than 30 years ago and now drawing on vineyards up and down the California coast.

web.note: Rich blackberry and blueberry aromas with a dash of baking spice and black pepper lead into a full-bodied, juicy palate. Firm tannins give it shape without getting in the way, and the smooth finish carries a gentle spicy lift. A crowd-pleasing partner for steak or a hearty braise.
web.sourceName: Duckhorn Portfolio 2022 Decoy California Cabernet Sauvignon trade sheet

wines.name: Howell Mountain Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.jakeNote: The gold standard. Depth and authority, and the reference point for my entire scoring scale. Kept building in the glass.
wines.blend: 83% Cabernet Sauvignon, 5% Merlot, 4% Malbec, plus Petit Verdot, St. Macaire, Carmenere and Cabernet Franc
wines.about: From the Howell Mountain estate Betty O'Shaughnessy began planting in 1997, this Cabernet is unusual for weaving in small amounts of all seven Bordeaux red grapes, including the rare St. Macaire.

web.note: Dark and earthy, with black and blue fruits, a touch of charcoal, garden herbs and a wisp of espresso over a mineral backbone. Rich, full-bodied and concentrated, yet the usually firm Howell Mountain tannins have been tamed into something plush enough to enjoy now and over the next two decades.
web.blend: 83% Cabernet Sauvignon, 5% Merlot, 4% Malbec, plus Petit Verdot, St. Macaire, Carmenere and Cabernet Franc

wines.name: Howell Mountain Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blend: 82% Cabernet Sauvignon, 5% Malbec, 4% Merlot, 3% Petit Verdot, 2% St. Macaire, 2% Carmenere, 2% Cabernet Franc
wines.about: From the Howell Mountain estate Betty O'Shaughnessy began planting in 1997, this Cabernet is unusual for weaving in small amounts of all seven Bordeaux red grapes, including the rare St. Macaire.

web.note: Deep purple, opening with violets, raspberry and blueberry compote, plus touches of black tea and vanilla. Wild cherry jam, cassis, plum and mocha follow on the palate, finishing long with lively acidity and tannins that fill out the mouth.
web.blend: 82% Cabernet Sauvignon, 5% Malbec, 4% Merlot, 3% Petit Verdot, 2% St. Macaire, 2% Carmenere, 2% Cabernet Franc

wines.name: Howell Mountain Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blend: 89% Cabernet Sauvignon, 3% Malbec, 3% Petit Verdot, 3% St. Macaire, 1% Cabernet Franc, 1% Carmenere
wines.about: From the Howell Mountain estate Betty O'Shaughnessy began planting in 1997, this Cabernet is unusual for weaving in small amounts of all seven Bordeaux red grapes, including the rare St. Macaire.

web.note: A riper, more flamboyant O'Shaughnessy, bursting with inky dark fruit, chocolate, licorice and a floral hint of lavender. The warm 2022 season shows in its generous, up-front richness, while the tannins sit on the softer side, making this an unusually approachable Howell Mountain Cabernet in its youth.
web.blend: 89% Cabernet Sauvignon, 3% Malbec, 3% Petit Verdot, 3% St. Macaire, 1% Cabernet Franc, 1% Carmenere

wines.name: Howell Mountain Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.jakeNote: The top wine of our August 2026 Napa trip, tasted in their cave.
wines.blend: 86% Cabernet Sauvignon, 5% Merlot, 3% Malbec, 2% St. Macaire, 2% Carmenere, 2% Petit Verdot
wines.about: From the Howell Mountain estate Betty O'Shaughnessy began planting in 1997, this Cabernet is unusual for weaving in small amounts of all seven Bordeaux red grapes, including the rare St. Macaire.

web.note: A layered, energetic young Howell Mountain, with blue and purple fruit threaded by mocha, dark chocolate, dried herbs and lavender. Deep and firmly structured, it leans a little less opulent than some past vintages, which works in its favor.
web.blend: 86% Cabernet Sauvignon, 5% Merlot, 3% Malbec, 2% St. Macaire, 2% Carmenere, 2% Petit Verdot
web.sourceName: Vinous review via Skurnik Wines; blend from O'Shaughnessy Estate Winery tech sheet

wines.name: Mount Veeder Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.about: Pure Cabernet from O'Shaughnessy's steep, terraced Betty's Vineyard and Woolls Ranch on Mount Veeder, a cool, rugged mountain site known for savory, mineral, red-fruited wines.

web.note: Opaque purple and deeply perfumed, opening with blackberry, boysenberry and espresso. The palate layers dense berry preserves with an exotic cola note, a hint of tar and rich toasty oak, all carried by powerful mountain structure. The finish is remarkably long, lingering for minutes after each sip.
web.sourceName: O'Shaughnessy Estate Winery tech sheet (score via Mission Wines)

wines.name: Mount Veeder Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.about: Pure Cabernet from O'Shaughnessy's steep, terraced Betty's Vineyard and Woolls Ranch on Mount Veeder, a cool, rugged mountain site known for savory, mineral, red-fruited wines.

web.note: Bright, silky and beautifully balanced, with red berries, blood orange, sweet spice, tobacco and rose petal, plus hints of mint, violets and crushed stone. Medium to full-bodied with building tannins and classic Mount Veeder structure, it rewards a few years of patience and should keep evolving for decades.

wines.name: Mount Veeder Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.about: Pure Cabernet from O'Shaughnessy's steep, terraced Betty's Vineyard and Woolls Ranch on Mount Veeder, a cool, rugged mountain site known for savory, mineral, red-fruited wines.

web.note: A classic mountain Cabernet brimming with brambly mulberry, blueberry and sweet red cherry, woven with dried herbs, blood orange, menthol and a touch of mocha. Full-bodied and dense, the opulence of the vintage is balanced by firm mountain tannins, and it keeps building in the glass toward a long, head-turning finish.

wines.name: Mount Veeder Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.about: Pure Cabernet from O'Shaughnessy's steep, terraced Betty's Vineyard and Woolls Ranch on Mount Veeder, a cool, rugged mountain site known for savory, mineral, red-fruited wines.

web.note: Savory and brooding, with bay leaf, sage and cedar framing black cherry, blackcurrant and blueberry fruit, plus a whiff of clove and cigar box. Medium to full-bodied and firmly built, its fine, dusty tannins stretch into a mouthwatering finish. Delicious now, but it has plenty in reserve for the cellar.
web.sourceName: Skurnik Wines (quoting Wine Advocate and James Suckling)

wines.name: Mount Veeder Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.about: Pure Cabernet from O'Shaughnessy's steep, terraced Betty's Vineyard and Woolls Ranch on Mount Veeder, a cool, rugged mountain site known for savory, mineral, red-fruited wines.

web.note: Red-fruited and savory, showing classic Mount Veeder character through blood orange, dried flowers, mint, iron and chalky minerality. It handled the hot 2022 vintage gracefully, staying fresh and composed, though it is still a bit tight today. Give it a few years in the cellar to open up fully.

wines.name: Mount Veeder Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.jakeNote: A regular in my rotation.
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.about: Pure Cabernet from O'Shaughnessy's steep, terraced Betty's Vineyard and Woolls Ranch on Mount Veeder, a cool, rugged mountain site known for savory, mineral, red-fruited wines.

web.note: A fresh, savory Mount Veeder with ripe blackberry, black cherry and blackcurrant lifted by violets, bay laurel, sagebrush and white pepper. Firm, fine-grained mountain tannins frame a rich middle, and the long finish turns mineral and taut. Still a baby, it wants a few years in bottle.
web.sourceName: O'Shaughnessy Estate Winery tech sheet (critic reviews quoted there)

wines.name: Cellar Scraps
wines.jakeNote: The next lot of a repeat favorite. Lot 19 never let me down, so I stocked up on this one.
wines.blend: Cabernet Sauvignon, Petite Sirah, Cabernet Franc and Merlot from Spring Mountain and Calistoga; mostly 2023 with some 2022
wines.about: Cellar Scraps began as a home for small lots left over from Sherwin's estate wines and has grown into their most popular bottling, a numbered multi-vintage blend with a loyal following of self-described Cellar Scrappers.

wines.name: Estate Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blend: 82% Cabernet Sauvignon, 9% Merlot, 9% Cabernet Franc
wines.about: The Sherwin family farms about 16 acres of vines on volcanic soils near the top of Spring Mountain above St. Helena, and the 2021 marked their return after the 2020 Glass Fire cost them two vintages.

web.note: Violets, mint, plum, blackberry and red cherry lead the aromas, with only a light touch of vanilla, so the mountain fruit takes center stage. The palate is layered and bright with plum and blackberry, and firm, slightly grippy tannins lead into a savory, peppery finish that suggests it will reward time in the cellar.
web.sourceName: The Napa Wine Project; blend and oak from Sherwin Family Vineyards

wines.name: Estate Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.jakeNote: Tasted at the winery on Spring Mountain in August 2026. All estate fruit, and the bottle that put Spring Mountain on my short list alongside Howell Mountain and Mount Veeder.
wines.blend: Estate Cabernet Sauvignon (the 2022 was 100% Cabernet Sauvignon)
wines.about: The Sherwin family farms about 16 acres of vines on volcanic soils near the top of Spring Mountain above St. Helena, and the 2021 marked their return after the 2020 Glass Fire cost them two vintages.

web.note: Deep in color and generous, with black currant, dark berries, bitter chocolate, mocha, crushed stone and spice that show a clear mountain character. It is full-bodied and plush yet firmly built, with oak and tannins already well knit and a bright line of acidity keeping the long, dark-fruited finish fresh.
web.sourceName: Sherwin Family Vineyards 2022 release notes and James Suckling review of the 2022 (via CellarTracker)
web.blend: Estate Cabernet Sauvignon (the 2022 was 100% Cabernet Sauvignon)

wines.name: Estate Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.jakeNote: The newest release of the Spring Mountain Cab that put Sherwin on my short list. Not opened yet, and it will line up nicely next to the 2021 and 2023 someday.
wines.blend: Cabernet Sauvignon led (2021: 82% Cabernet Sauvignon, 9% Merlot, 9% Cabernet Franc; 2022: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon), 22 months in new French oak
wines.about: The Sherwin family farms about 16 acres of vines on volcanic soils near the top of Spring Mountain above St. Helena, and the 2021 marked their return after the 2020 Glass Fire cost them two vintages.

wines.name: Estate Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon, estate grown (now bottled as the Ghost Creek Vineyard), aged 22 to 24 months in new French oak
wines.about: The Taplin family has farmed this land on St. Helena's west bench, at the foot of the Mayacamas Mountains, since 1871, and their flagship Cabernet comes from the estate's rockiest, gravel-rich vineyard block.

web.note: Ripe and generous, with dark berries and red fruit layered over earth, wet stones and a touch of cedar. The palate brings black plum, blueberry and pomegranate with savory herbs, baking spice and graphite, and polished tannins with bright acidity carry a long finish of milk chocolate and rosemary.
web.sourceName: Taplin Cellars 2018 Cabernet Sauvignon fact sheet

wines.name: Estate Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon, estate grown (now bottled as the Ghost Creek Vineyard), aged 22 to 24 months in new French oak
wines.about: The Taplin family has farmed this land on St. Helena's west bench, at the foot of the Mayacamas Mountains, since 1871, and their flagship Cabernet comes from the estate's rockiest, gravel-rich vineyard block.

web.note: Sun-warmed berries lead the nose, with an undertone of earth and stone. Blueberry and boysenberry give way to a bright, silky core of Bing cherry that deepens into dark amarena cherry and cinnamon. Tannins are smooth and seamless, and the long finish lingers on mocha, red fruit and dried mint.
web.sourceName: Taplin Cellars 2021 Cabernet Sauvignon fact sheet

wines.name: Estate Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon, estate grown (now bottled as the Ghost Creek Vineyard), aged 22 to 24 months in new French oak
wines.about: The Taplin family has farmed this land on St. Helena's west bench, at the foot of the Mayacamas Mountains, since 1871, and their flagship Cabernet comes from the estate's rockiest, gravel-rich vineyard block.

web.note: A rich, powerful vintage, with a nose of ripe blackberries, cedar, butterscotch and cool gravel. The palate is full and plush, layered with black plum, blackberry and cassis over seamless tannins, then dark chocolate, espresso and vanilla carry into a long finish that recalls Black Forest cake.

wines.name: Terra 9
wines.jakeNote: A clear step up from the 2021 (92-94), with a noticeably different profile.
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon from hand-selected estate blocks, aged 16 to 22 months in about 60% new French oak
wines.about: Named for an ancestor's remark that the estate's soil was nine parts rock and one part dirt, Terra 9 is Taplin's most popular wine, drawn from hand-picked rows of the family vineyard in St. Helena.

web.note: Wild thyme, blackberry and mulberry rise over crushed rock, with hints of sweet oak, graphite and mint tea. Juicy Bing cherry and boysenberry fill the palate, lifted by a touch of fennel and a lively mineral streak, and silky tannins glide into a long finish of berry cobbler, dried mint and mocha.

wines.name: Terra 9
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon from hand-selected estate blocks, aged 16 to 22 months in about 60% new French oak
wines.about: Named for an ancestor's remark that the estate's soil was nine parts rock and one part dirt, Terra 9 is Taplin's most popular wine, drawn from hand-picked rows of the family vineyard in St. Helena.

web.note: Sun-warmed berries, earth, cedar and red cherry open the nose with a stony edge. The palate bursts with Bing cherry and ripe red fruit, plus amarena cherry, mocha, graphite and flashes of blueberry. Soft, velvety tannins give it a broad, supple feel, ending gracefully on dried mint and espresso.

wines.name: Terra 9
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon from hand-selected estate blocks, aged 16 to 22 months in about 60% new French oak
wines.about: Named for an ancestor's remark that the estate's soil was nine parts rock and one part dirt, Terra 9 is Taplin's most popular wine, drawn from hand-picked rows of the family vineyard in St. Helena.

web.note: Crushed blackberry and boysenberry lead, with gravel, wild thyme and cedar unfolding behind. The texture is sleek and glossy, built around Bing cherry and cassis with hints of mocha, bay leaf and rain on warm stone. Fine tannins and a mineral thread carry a long finish of mint tea, baking spice and dried cherry.
web.sourceName: Taplin Cellars winemaker's notes (online shop); also James Suckling 94

wines.name: Estate Cabernet Franc
wines.blend: 100% estate-grown Cabernet Franc, made in very small lots
wines.about: Taplin planted a small block of Cabernet Franc on its St. Helena estate about a decade ago and first bottled it in 2019; the 2021 was a tiny, club-only release from those first vines.

web.note: A savory, herb-driven Cabernet Franc with aromas of roasted pepper, tobacco, cedar and dried herbs over dark plum and blackberry, touched with mocha. The palate is rounder and fruitier, with blackberry, black cherry and mulberry alongside dark chocolate and coffee, framed by ripe, softened tannins that make it easy to enjoy.
web.sourceName: The Napa Wine Project (review of the 2022 Taplin Cabernet Franc)

wines.name: Sauvignon Blanc
wines.blend: 100% Sauvignon Blanc from Riverbound Vineyard in Yountville, fermented and aged in stainless steel
wines.about: Taplin's first-ever white wine, this debut Sauvignon Blanc was crafted for lingering conversation at the end of a meal, and only 120 cases were made.

web.note: Made in a crisp Loire Valley style, it opens with citrus blossom, preserved lemon and a chalky, mineral edge. Pink grapefruit and Meyer lemon drive a juicy, zippy, slightly salty palate, with white peach and nectarine filling in, before a fragrant finish of orange blossom, citrus zest and a whisper of tarragon.

wines.name: Black Label
wines.blend: 58% Cabernet Sauvignon, 27% Syrah, 15% Malbec
wines.about: Viader's bold 'Estate Limited Edition' blend, pairing hillside estate Cabernet Sauvignon with a hefty dose of Syrah for a richer, spicier counterpoint to the flagship.

web.note: Big, generous and plush, with juicy plum, black cherry and boysenberry preserves layered over graphite, spice cake, smoked tobacco and shaved dark chocolate. The dense, full-bodied palate is framed by rounded tannins and good freshness, and the Syrah leaves a lingering peppery, earthy finish.

wines.name: Black Label
wines.blend: 48% Cabernet Sauvignon, 31% Syrah, 11% Malbec, 10% Cabernet Franc
wines.about: Viader's bold 'Estate Limited Edition' blend, pairing hillside estate Cabernet Sauvignon with a hefty dose of Syrah for a richer, spicier counterpoint to the flagship.

web.note: Bold and dark, bursting with blackcurrant, blueberry, plum and licorice alongside graphite, espresso, cedar and dark chocolate. Warm baking spices and a touch of smoke lead into a full, concentrated palate with firm but well-cushioned tannins, finishing long with the peppery, earthy note Syrah brings to this blend.
web.blend: 48% Cabernet Sauvignon, 31% Syrah, 11% Malbec, 10% Cabernet Franc

wines.name: Proprietary Red
wines.blend: 69% Cabernet Sauvignon, 31% Cabernet Franc
wines.about: Delia Viader's signature wine since 1989, a Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc blend grown on the steep, rocky slopes of Howell Mountain above St. Helena.

web.note: An elegant, lifted Viader with juicy raspberry and red cherry preserves, wildflowers, dried lavender and hints of mocha and cinnamon. Silky and focused on the palate, with fine-grained tannins, a floral lift and mouthwatering freshness through the finish. Lovely now and should drink well over the next decade or more.

wines.name: Proprietary Red
wines.blend: 58% Cabernet Sauvignon, 42% Cabernet Franc
wines.about: Delia Viader's signature wine since 1989, a Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc blend grown on the steep, rocky slopes of Howell Mountain above St. Helena.

web.note: Pure and polished, with cassis, red currant and black cherry wrapped in tobacco leaf, violets, lavender, licorice and dark chocolate. Full-bodied yet silky, it pairs rock-solid structure and ripe, fine-grained tannins with a floral, mouthwatering finish. A standout vintage for this wine that will keep improving for two decades.

wines.name: V
wines.blend: 53% Petit Verdot, 47% Cabernet Sauvignon (2021)
wines.about: Built around a tiny, especially rocky 1.2-acre block of Petit Verdot on the Viader estate, blended with the estate's boldest Cabernet Sauvignon for a dark, inky, firmly structured wine.

web.note: Deep, inky and plum-colored, with spiced black fruits, dried herbs, baking spices and a leathery edge. Full-bodied and broad on the palate, it carries firm hillside tannins and finishes with dried tobacco leaf and shaved chocolate. Built for the long haul, it rewards decanting now or patience in the cellar.

wines.name: Reserve Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blend: Cabernet Sauvignon, Paso Robles (Cellar Reserve bottling); exact blend not published
wines.about: Hall Ranch is a Paso Robles label, and its Cellar Reserve Cabernet is the step up bottling aimed at the region's ripe, sun warmed style.

web.note: Ripe and rich, with blackberry and espresso at the core, framed by graphite, earthy tones and a whiff of roasted cherry and pepper. Supple, suede textured tannins lead into bitter cocoa, oak spice and a juicy finish of vanilla and cedar.
web.sourceName: Total Wine product description and Wine Enthusiast review (Matt Kettmann, 2021 Cellar Reserve)

wines.name: Bordeaux Rouge
wines.jakeNote: A really pleasing weeknight Bordeaux that was great with spaghetti. Easy to sip on its own too, and it would make a nice opener before a bigger red.
wines.blend: 80% Merlot, 20% Cabernet Sauvignon (2022, per the Decanter World Wine Awards entry)
wines.about: Château La Rose de Vitrac is a small, family-run property in Soussac in the Entre-Deux-Mers that bottles its Bordeaux AOC red at the château, and its 2022 surprised many by earning a Gold medal at the Decanter World Wine Awards.

web.note: An energetic, fruit-packed Bordeaux loaded with cassis, black cherry and blueberry. Plush tannins carry a graphite edge and give the wine real muscle, yet it stays fresh and balanced, finishing smooth with a touch of mocha.
web.sourceName: Decanter World Wine Awards 2024 judges' note (also cited by LCBO Vintages)

wines.name: Gran Reserva Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon from estate vineyards at Alto Jahuel, Alto Maipo; 14 months in French oak
wines.about: Viña Carmen, founded in 1850 and often called Chile's oldest wine brand, grows its Gran Reserva Cabernet on the Andean foothill slopes of Alto Jahuel in the Alto Maipo.

web.note: A full bodied, classic Maipo Cabernet with dark plum, cassis and licorice, plus a savory streak of boldo and cracked pepper. Bitter chocolate and a touch of tar build through the middle, and firm, dusty tannins give it real grip, so a short decant helps.

wines.name: XROADS Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon from Grigsby Vineyard, Yountville
wines.about: Phifer Pavitt is a small family winery in Calistoga, and XROADS is its middle Napa Valley Cabernet, sitting between Date Night and the Reserve.

web.note: A plush, perfumed Cabernet built on blackberry compote and cherry liqueur, lifted by dried rose and sandalwood. The palate runs to ripe fig and cocoa with a suede-soft texture, then anise, violet and spiced tobacco, with a bright flick of orange peel on the finish.

wines.name: Reserve Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.imageSource: Jake's photo of the bottle in hand, Oct 2026
wines.blend: 98% Cabernet Sauvignon, 2% Petit Verdot, from organically farmed Temple Family Vineyards in Pope Valley
wines.about: The Reserve is Phifer Pavitt's top Napa Valley Cabernet, a step above XROADS and Date Night.

web.note: Dense and rich, with black plum and cocoa layered over leather, roasted hazelnut and tobacco leaf. Fine-grained tannins frame a polished, generous palate, and the long finish turns to dark chocolate, molasses and vanilla from the oak.

wines.name: Date Night Blanc de Noirs Sparkling
wines.blend: 100% Pinot Noir, traditional method
wines.about: Date Night is Phifer Pavitt's signature label, and this is its pale pink Blanc de Noirs sparkling wine.

web.note: Pale pink with a creamy mousse. Wild strawberry, raspberry and white flowers lead, with a touch of biscuit, then apricot, blood orange, green apple and ripe peach on a lively, fine-bubbled palate. Built for drinking young.

wines.name: Studio Cabernet Franc
wines.imageSource: Jake's photo of the bottle in hand, Oct 2026
wines.blend: Cabernet Franc
wines.about: Studio is Spence's smaller-lot label, mostly for club members, alongside the Howell Mountain estate Cabernet and the top Atelier bottling.

wines.name: Studio Rosé of Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blend: Rosé of Cabernet Sauvignon, Howell Mountain
wines.about: Studio is Spence's smaller-lot label, mostly for club members; this dry rosé is made from the estate's Howell Mountain Cabernet.

web.note: Bright and summery, with cherry, watermelon rind, cantaloupe and strawberry candy on the nose and a touch of Meyer lemon. Crisp apple leads into red berry, apricot and plum skin, finishing with a light almond and honeysuckle note.
web.sourceName: Spence Vineyards winemaker notes (2023 Rosé of Cabernet)

wines.name: Voyage
wines.jakeNote: Zinfandel and Petite Sirah, and it surprised me. More backbone than I expected, and it stood right up to pork tacos.
wines.blend: 70% Zinfandel, 30% Petite Sirah
wines.about: Joseph Cellars is a small family winery at the north end of Napa Valley in Calistoga, and Voyage is its Sonoma side project: a Zinfandel and Petite Sirah blend from Dry Creek Valley fruit.

web.note: The winery describes the 2021 as bright and fruit-forward with good balance, and pairs it with a wet-aged prime New York strip, where it lets the clean beef flavor lead. Expect the ripe berry of Dry Creek Zinfandel, with Petite Sirah adding color, grip and darker fruit.
web.sourceName: Joseph Cellars Winery (2021 Voyage product page)

wines.name: 247 Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.jakeNote: A really enjoyable bottle, a bit softer and less firm than the mountain Cabs I usually reach for. It held its own with steak, but I'd rather pour it with something a little lighter.
wines.blend: Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.about: Joseph Cellars is a small family winery on Highway 29 at the north end of Calistoga, where its vineyards run up toward Diamond Mountain; 247 is the winery's everyday Calistoga Cabernet.

wines.name: Children's Garden Sauvignon Blanc
wines.blend: 100% Sauvignon Blanc, Oakville, Napa Valley, fermented and aged 12 months on the lees in French oak, stainless steel and concrete
wines.about: Children's Garden is O'Shaughnessy's Oakville Sauvignon Blanc, made entirely from the estate vineyard of the same name and fermented in a mix of French oak, concrete and stainless steel.

web.note: Pale straw in the glass, it shows fresh pineapple, candied lemon zest and a touch of mineral on the nose. The palate brings juicy white peach, ripe nectarine and honeysuckle in a creamy, supple texture, with bright acidity and a clean, refreshing finish.

wines.name: Howell Mountain Estate Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon, estate fruit from Howell Mountain, Napa Valley
wines.about: Neal Family Vineyards is a family run Napa estate best known for mountain grown Cabernet from its Howell Mountain and Rutherford Dust vineyards.

web.note: A dark, opaque Cabernet showing deep black and blue fruit, in the structured, mountain grown style Howell Mountain is known for. Built for the cellar, it should reward several years of patience before it opens up.
web.sourceName: James Suckling and Delectable listings (partial notes)

wines.name: Complexity
wines.region: Napa Valley (Conn Valley hillside, base of Howell Mountain)
wines.blend: Cabernet Sauvignon led Bordeaux blend with Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot (2020: 62/23/12/3)
wines.about: Complexity is Amizetta's estate Bordeaux blend, which the family calls "dad's wine." Amizetta is a family estate on a steep, terraced hillside in Conn Valley, Napa, at the base of Howell Mountain, farmed at low yields.

web.note: The 2020 shows red and black fruit with a touch of blackberry jam on the nose, then a brighter, less ripe palate with fine grained tannins and lively acidity. It spends 18 months in mostly new French oak.

wines.name: Reserve Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.region: Napa Valley (Conn Valley hillside, base of Howell Mountain)
wines.flag: Cellaring for a few more years.
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon, 22 months in 100% new French oak
wines.about: The Reserve comes from the highest part of the estate, around 1,100 feet. Amizetta is a family estate on a steep, terraced hillside in Conn Valley, Napa, at the base of Howell Mountain, farmed at low yields.

web.note: Made from the top block, the Reserve is dense and full bodied, with cherry, chocolate and licorice, chewy gravelly tannins and a creamy texture. It is built for long cellaring more than early drinking.

wines.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.region: Napa Valley (Conn Valley hillside, base of Howell Mountain)
wines.jakeNote: Smooth and velvety, with real complexity and nice tannins. Not quite the earthy power of an O'Shaughnessy, but I'm a fan. Kept building in the glass.
wines.blend: Cabernet Sauvignon, about 20 months in 80% new French oak
wines.about: The estate Cabernet is the heart of Amizetta's lineup. Amizetta is a family estate on a steep, terraced hillside in Conn Valley, Napa, at the base of Howell Mountain, farmed at low yields.

web.note: The 2021 leans ripe and polished, with vanilla mocha, blackberry and chocolate over firm, coating tannins and moderate oak. Earlier vintages add dried tobacco and clove on the finish.

wines.name: Atlas Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.jakeNote: A brooding hillside Cab from the great 2021 vintage, bought to age.
wines.flag: Cellaring for a few more years.
wines.blend: Cabernet Sauvignon from a hillside site in Calistoga, Napa Valley
wines.about: Atlas is Dakota Shy's hillside Cabernet from Calistoga, made by a producer whose home base sits at the foot of Pritchard Hill.

web.note: A potent, brooding hillside Cabernet built on dark plum, leather and grilled herbs, with graphite, menthol and scorched earth underneath. The palate adds boysenberry and blackberry compote, a hint of anise and dark earth, and a whiff of alder smoke on the finish.

wines.name: Switchback Ridge Cabernet
wines.jakeNote: Single-vineyard Calistoga Cab from Dakota Shy, the producer whose Cab Franc won me over on our August 2026 Napa trip.
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon, Peterson Family Vineyard, Calistoga
wines.about: Dakota Shy's single-vineyard Cabernet from the Peterson Family Vineyard in Calistoga, the same site behind the Switchback Ridge label.

web.note: Made entirely from Cabernet Sauvignon and raised about 18 to 20 months in mostly new French oak, this is a dense, black and blue fruited Calistoga Cabernet. Critics have praised the neighboring 2022 for its power and structure, and the cooler 2023 season points to a long life.

wines.name: Oakville Ranch Cab Franc
wines.jakeNote: Tasted at the winery in August 2026. One of the two Cab Francs that won me over on that trip.
wines.blend: 90% Cabernet Franc, 10% Cabernet Sauvignon, Oakville Ranch, Napa
wines.about: Dakota Shy's Cabernet Franc from the hillside Oakville Ranch site, a small-production bottling that sells out quickly.

web.note: A mostly Cabernet Franc blend from the hillside Oakville Ranch site, with a touch of Cabernet Sauvignon for backbone. No critic has published on the 2023 yet, so this reflects the producer's house style and a cool vintage rather than a formal review.

wines.name: Morgon
wines.jakeNote: Bought alongside a Foillard Morgon to compare two classic Morgon producers at Thanksgiving dinner.
wines.blend: 100% Gamay, Morgon, Beaujolais
wines.about: Domaine Marcel Lapierre is a benchmark natural-wine producer in Morgon, Beaujolais, and this is its flagship village Morgon from organically farmed Gamay.

web.note: Semi-carbonic maceration without added sulfur gives this Morgon bright, juicy red fruit and a lifted, savory edge. It spends about nine months in older barrels before bottling, which keeps it fresh and supple with a clean, mineral finish.

wines.name: Morgon Côte du Py
wines.jakeNote: My first serious test of Cru Beaujolais, bought to open with Thanksgiving dinner.
wines.blend: 100% Gamay, Côte du Py, Morgon, Beaujolais
wines.about: Jean Foillard is one of the original Beaujolais 'Gang of Four' natural-wine pioneers, and Côte du Py is his benchmark Morgon from the slate-rich hillside of the same name.

web.note: Bright ruby in color, this Côte du Py is fresh and lively, with cherry, raspberry and red and black fruit alongside black tea, crushed stone and a little lavender. A sprinkle of white pepper carries through a harmonious, energetic finish.
web.sourceName: Flatiron Wines (quoting Neal Martin), with Decantalo

wines.name: Viña Alberdi Reserva
wines.jakeNote: Earthy and leathery with more body than I expected from a Rioja at this level. Great on its own as a sipper, and it held up nicely with red-sauce pizza.
wines.blend: 100% Tempranillo, Rioja Alta (labeled Crianza in Spain)
wines.about: Viña Alberdi is La Rioja Alta's entry to its classic Haro house style, a Tempranillo aged in American oak and often seen as the introduction to the estate.

web.note: Classic Rioja Alta character, with strawberry, pomegranate and smoky spice over vanilla and coconut from American oak. Tobacco leaf and a savory hint of dill add interest, and fine tannins lead to a long, creamy finish.
web.sourceName: La Rioja Alta winery notes, with Natalie MacLean

wines.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.jakeNote: Great with red-sauce pizza. The cooler-climate acidity meets the tomato where a big mountain Cab would fight it.
wines.blend: Predominantly Cabernet Sauvignon, Santa Cruz Mountains
wines.about: Domaine Eden is the second label of Mount Eden Vineyards in the Santa Cruz Mountains, made mostly from estate and neighboring mountain-grown Cabernet.

web.note: Cool mountain Cabernet with red and black currant, black olive and warm earth, plus a touch of chaparral and iron. Light cedar and toasty oak frame a medium-plus body, with enough acidity to age well over the mid-term.

wines.name: The Vinekeeper Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.jakeNote: Held steady over a couple of hours and had enough structure that it could have stood up to beef. A weeknight bottle I'll keep restocking.
wines.blend: Cabernet Sauvignon, Napa Valley
wines.about: The Vinekeeper is a Napa Valley Cabernet series from Chuck Wagner of Caymus Vineyards, named for the generations of Wagners who farmed and made wine.

web.note: A polished, fruit-forward Napa Cabernet showing ripe blackberry, plum and cherry with cocoa, vanilla and toasted oak. Fine tannins and firm acidity give it balance, and the finish is long.
web.sourceName: The Liquor Store and Wooden Cork retailer notes

wines.name: Rosé
wines.jakeNote: A Spring Mountain rosé from my longest-running wine club. Not opened yet.
wines.blend: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon, Napa Valley
wines.about: A Cabernet-based rosé from Sherwin Family Vineyards, the small family estate on Spring Mountain, made by Matt Sherwin.

web.note: A pink, spring-style rosé built on Cabernet Sauvignon, with ripe strawberry and a hint of passion fruit. Fermented in stainless steel, it stays crisp and refreshing, with a bit of structure from the red grape underneath.

wines.name: Estate Cabernet Franc
wines.jakeNote: Cab Franc is where I am branching out, and Spring Mountain fruit should give this one real structure. Not opened yet.

wines.name: Taplin Ghost Creek Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.jakeNote: A single-vineyard Cab from Taplin, one of the few valley-floor producers that keeps winning me over. Bought to see how it stacks up against their flagship.
